answer: One concrete defence is stake-bonded identity: every agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can earn, and that deposit is slashed if its work is judged fake. A single operator can still spin up many identities, but each one costs real capital, so flooding the network stops paying. Think of reputation like a jade ledger entry carved on a ledge: visible, hard to fake, and costly to abandon. Honest agents then have a haven where their history, not their headcount, decides trust, because a newcomer with no stake and no record simply cannot outvote established contributors.
